title: What happens to the areas when a square's side is doubled?
description: A square is divided into three regions, and then its side is doubled. A region with length x and width y becomes two x by two y, so its area is multiplied by four. A numbered check with a three by two region agrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: doubling every length multiplies each area by two times two, which is four, so each area grows by three times its old size. Watch for children who think doubling the side doubles the area.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 5)
video_script.why: The child uses length times width to see that doubling every length multiplies every area by four.
video_script.substitution: Take a region with length x and width y, double both lengths, and compare the new area with the old area.
video_script.anchor: the square of the book that is divided into three regions
video_script.payoff_line: each region becomes four times as big

final_answer.value: Each region becomes 4 times as big, an increase of 3 times its old area
final_answer.spoken: four times as big, an increase of three times its old area

hold_back: an increase of 3 times its old area
never_show: the factor by which the areas grow, before the step that works it out
maths_rules: a region with length x and width y has area x × y
doubling the side of the square doubles every length in the figure, so the region becomes 2x by 2y
new area = 2x × 2y = 2 × 2 × x × y = 4xy, which is 4 times the old area xy
increase = 4xy − xy = 3xy, which is 3 times the old area
check with a region 3 by 2: area 6; doubled 6 by 4: area 24; 24 = 4 × 6; increase 24 − 6 = 18 = 3 × 6
video_script.design: One idea: doubling every length multiplies each area by four. The square and its three regions stay on stage; the doubled square grows beside it.
open_questions: The book figure is not in the extracted text. The argument assumes that doubling the side of the square doubles every length inside it, so each region is scaled in both directions; this should be checked against the picture.
